last.summary: Fixed the review finding in projects/bzip2/spec/Bzip2/Spec/Format.lean. readDelta now does the `1 <= curr <= 20` check before anything else (decompress.c:326-328: range check, then GET_BIT). Fuel is only a termination bound, used after the bit reads; it can run out only after readBit has already failed. readSymbols had the same flaw: it reported EOF before the selector check (decompress.c:76-79 checks groupNo >= nSelectors before GET_BITS). It now looks up the selector first and uses fuel only for recursion. Added four `decide +kernel` examples. (1) The reviewer's 25-byte stream ending right after a 5-bit curr of 0 gives `.error .data`, and its 24-byte prefix gives `.error .eof`. (2) A 35-byte stream with one selector and 50 one-bit symbols ending on the group boundary gives `.error .data`, and its 34-byte prefix gives `.error .eof`. I built the vendored upstream out of tree (/tmp) and ran `bzip2 -dc` on all four inputs: 'Data integrity error when decompressing' for both full streams and 'Compressed file ends unexpectedly' for both prefixes, all exit 2. Checks: `sh -c 'projects/bzip2/tools/verify.sh && projects/bzip2/tools/check-task.sh spec/format'` printed `verify: packages: ok`, `verify: sources: ok`, `verify: build: ok`, `verify: style: ok`, `verify: axioms: ok`, `verify: lint: ok`, `verify: test: ok`, `verify: ok`, `check-task: spec/format: ok`. `git status` is clean, and `git diff --stat origin/master...HEAD` shows only projects/bzip2/spec/Bzip2/Spec/Format.lean.
